BURSEVI:v10p386/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p386/r1.claim: The person whose weighed qualities are divine attributes and godly character traits is at rest from the consequences of those qualities.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r1.anchor: فأما من ثقلت له موزونات الأوصاف الإلهية والأخلاق اللاهوتية فهو في راحة واستراحة

BURSEVI:v10p386/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r2.claim: Scales are light when a person has no good deed of weight or when sins outweigh good deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r2.anchor: بأن لم يكن له حسنة يعتد بها أو ترجحت سيئاته على حسناته

BURSEVI:v10p386/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p386/r3.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud says one extra good deed leads to Paradise, while one extra bad deed leads to Hell.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r3.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه يحاسب الناس يوم القيامة فمن كانت حسناته أكثر من سيئاته بواحدة دخل الجنة

BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.claim: The inward reading makes the origin of those with light scales an abyss of veiling and a hot fire of ignorance, blindness, ego, passion, Satan, and the world.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r9.anchor: فأصله المجبول عليه هاوية الحجاب من الأزل إلى الأبد وهي نار حامية بنار الجهل والعمى

BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.claim: Both groups commit sins, though the first has fewer and outweighed sins and the second has many; the trial remains, so the Prophet tells ‘Ali to follow a bad deed with a good one, in keeping with God's forgiving name.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r10.anchor: لعلي رضي الله عنه يا علي إذا عملت سيئة فاعمل بجنبها حسنة

BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.claim: God's scale reverses ordinary scales: rising and elevation are heaviness, while falling is lightness; weighty deeds are enduring good works, and valueless light deeds are passing sensual pleasures.
BURSEVI:v10p386/r11.anchor: اعلم أن ميزان الحق بخلاف ميزان الخلق إذ صعود الموزونات وارتفاعها فيه هو الثقل

QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.claim: Light scales are evil deeds and psychic vices; their owner’s home is the abyss of bodily nature’s hell.
QASHANI:101:6-10/r2.anchor: بأن كانت من الأعمال السيئة والرذائل النفسانية { فأمه هاوية }

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.claim: Only deeds will help: God weighs them in a just balance, granting eternal bliss when good deeds outweigh evil and Hell when the scales tip the other way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.anchor: God will set up the Balance of Justice in which all of man’s deeds will be weighed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.claim: The balance gives weight only to truth, meaning good deeds; the light-scaled lose because they denied God’s revelations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.anchor: On that day, the truth only will have weight.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.claim: The relative singular man in the scale descriptions denotes a plural group.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.anchor: as used in the verse above denotes plurality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.claim: Those whose evil deeds have no weight face eternal Hell; any good deeds are nullified by ill intent and heretical belief, and the next verse identifies the abyss as blazing fire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r4.anchor: due to their ill-int entions and heretical beliefs.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#3/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#3/r1.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says even a huge, tall, voracious man weighs no more than a gnat's wing before God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p392#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عيينة عن عمرو بن دينار عن عبيد بن عمير في قوله ﴿ وأما من خفت موازينه ﴾ قال يؤتى بالرجل العظيم الطويل الأكول الشروب

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r11.claim: Those whose scales are light in acts of obedience are the disbelievers, whose abode is the abyss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.claim: The author points back to earlier discussion of the weighing and to the description of a pleasing life in Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف، وعيشة راضية في الحاقة.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#2/r1.claim: Light scales mean either that a person has no good deed of consequence or that sins outweigh good deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p222#2/r1.anchor: بان لم يكن له حسنة يعتد بها أو ثقلت سيآته على حسناته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r1.claim: Light scales mean that a person's evil deeds outweigh the good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p514/r1.anchor: {وأما من خفت موازينه} رجحت سيئاته على حسناته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r6.claim: Light scales mean no worthy good deed exists or evil deeds outweigh good ones.
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r6.anchor: { وأما من خفت موزينه } بأن لم يكن له حسنة يعبأ بها، أو ترجحت سيئاته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.claim: Light scales mean evil deeds prevail or the person has no good deed because they followed falsehood; their refuge is the Hawiya, a very low, fiery abyss.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r5.anchor: بأن غلبت سيئاته أو لم تكن له حسنة لاتباعه الباطل وخفته عليه في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.claim: Hawiya is a sheltering abode, like a mother or the earth one returns to; the sinner continually falls through its depths, and the omitted clauses form an antithetical ellipsis.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r6.anchor: أي التي تؤويه وتضمه إليها كما يقال للأرض : أم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r11.speaker: المؤمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r11.claim: A believer's balance never becomes ruinously light.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p516#3/r11.anchor: ولن يخف خفة موبقة ميزان مؤمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r7.claim: A person whose bad deeds outweigh their good deeds has light scales.

MUQATIL:101:7-8/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r2.claim: The light scales belong to shirk: its good deeds become ash scattered by wind, leaving nothing to weigh; it is the foulest thing and the lightest in the balance.
MUQATIL:101:7-8/r2.anchor: وهو الشرك لأنه لا يرى شيئا مما كسب إلا صار كالرماد، فاشتدت به الريح

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#8/r1.claim: The scales are light because the person followed falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ وأما من خفت موازينه ﴾ باتباعهم الباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r1.claim: The balance has a pan and a tongue on which written records of good and bad deeds are weighed; Qurtubi discussed it under earlier surahs and in his Remembrance book.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r1.anchor: وأن له كفة ولسانا توزن فيه الصحف المكتوب فيها الحسنات والسيئات

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r2.claim: One interpretation says there is a single balance in Gabriel's hand weighing human deeds, expressed in plural form.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r2.anchor: ثم قيل: إنه ميزان واحد بيد جبريل يزن أعمال بني آدم، فعبر عنه بلفظ الجمع.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r3.claim: Another interpretation posits multiple balances, supported by a poet's line about each event having its balance.

QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r4.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r4.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya takes the balances as proofs and arguments, citing a poet who says he had a balance for every disputant.
QURTUBI-FULL:101:7-9/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن الموازين الحجج والدلائل، قاله عبد العزيز بن يحيى،

QUTB-ZILAL:101:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:101:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:101:8/r1.claim: Light scales refer to values that carry no weight in God’s judgment and assessment.

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r1.claim: Light scales mean few good deeds, with wrongs outweighing right actions.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r1.anchor: أي قلت : حسناته فرجحت السيئات على الحسنات

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r2.claim: Abu Bakr says the scale grows heavy through following the weighty truth in life, and grows light through following falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه : إنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينه

RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70#3/r3.claim: Al-Razi relays Muqatils explanation that truth is heavy and falsehood light.

STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.claim: The final six verses contrast the recompense of those whose scales are heavy with good deeds and those whose scales are light.
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.anchor: The last six verses (vv. 6–11) contrast the recompense

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.claim: Mawāzīn is plural of mīzān: the Qur'an uses balance for revelation and revealed just order, but scales for weighing deeds at Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.anchor: is employed in the Quran to indicate revelation itself

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.claim: Although the plural suggests each person's experience of weighing, most say one scale weighs all deeds.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.anchor: The plural, scales, speaks to how each individual will experience the weighing of his or her deeds, but according to most, it is in fact one scale

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.claim: Good and evil deeds are unequal; good deeds remove evil deeds, and a good deed earns tenfold while an evil deed is repaid only in kind.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.anchor: From a Quranic perspective, the good deed and the evil deed are not equal (41:34), and good deeds remove those that are evil (11:114).

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.claim: A hadith says nothing placed in the Balance weighs more heavily than good character.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.anchor: There is nothing placed in the Balance that is heavier than goodness of character

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.claim: A hadith says deeds are judged according to intentions, and each person receives what was intended.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.anchor: another ḥadīth states, “Deeds are only in accord with their intentions. And every person has only what he intended.”

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.claim: A hadith says no one enters Paradise through deeds alone; when asked whether this included him, the Prophet said only God's mercy would shelter him.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.anchor: As a ḥadīth states, “None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds.” Someone asked, “Not even you, O Messenger of God?”

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.claim: The light scales and abyss are linked to 7:9 and 23:103.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r9.anchor: For one whose scales are light, cf. 7:9; 23:103.

TAB:101:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:101:8/r1.claim: Those whose good deeds weigh little have the Hawiya as their abode, where they fall headfirst in Hell.
TAB:101:8/r1.anchor: يقول :  وأما من خفّ وزن حسناته ،   فمأواه ومسكنه الهاوية ،   التي يهوي فيها على رأسه في جهنم

TAB:101:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:101:8/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Hawiya is the Fire, the sinners' refuge; the phrase can also be an Arabic exclamation for a person in dire trouble.
TAB:101:8/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {  وَأمّا مَنْ خَفّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فأُمّهُ هاويَةٌ } وهي النار ،   هي مأواهم

TAB:101:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:101:8/r3.claim: Qatāda explains هوت أمه as a familiar Arabic phrase used when someone faces a severe predicament.
TAB:101:8/r3.anchor: قال قتادة :  هي كلمة عربية ،   كان الرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد ،   قال :  هوت أمه

TAB:101:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r4.speaker: الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى
TAB:101:8/r4.claim: Al-Ashʿath describes believers' spirits welcoming a dead believer from worldly grief; asked about the dead, they say they were taken to their mother, the Hawiya.
TAB:101:8/r4.anchor: عن الأشعث بن عبد الله الأعمى ،   قال :  إذا مات المؤمن ذهب بروحه إلى أرواح المؤمنين ،   فيقولون :  رَوّحوا أخاكم

TAB:101:8/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB:101:8/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says they fall headfirst into the Fire.
TAB:101:8/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح ،   في قوله {  فَأُمّهُ هاوِيَةٌ } قال :  يهوُون في النار على رؤوسهم

TAB:101:8/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:101:8/r6.claim: Qatāda also says the person falls into the Fire headfirst.
TAB:101:8/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {  فَأُمّهُ هاوِيَةٌ } قال :  يهوى في النار على رأسه

TAB:101:8/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:101:8/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that the Fire is called the person's mother because it is his refuge and the place to which he returns.
TAB:101:8/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  {  فَأُمّهُ هاوِيَةٌ } قال :  الهاوية :  النار هي أمّه ومأواه التي يرجع إليها

TAB:101:8/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:8/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:101:8/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Fire is made his mother because, with no other home, it shelters him as a woman shelters her child.
TAB:101:8/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {  فَأُمّهُ هاوِيَةٌ } وهو مثلها ،   وإنما جعل النار أمّه ؛  لأنها صارت مأواه ،   كما تؤوي المرأة ابنها

ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Meccan surah, probably revealed after At-Tin (surah 95).
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.anchor: An early Meccan surah, most probably revealed after surah 95 (At-Tin)

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.claim: The Meccan surah warns and gives glad tidings about resurrection, with warning as its dominant tone.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.anchor: بيان إنذار وتبشير بالقيامة يغلب فيه جانب الانذار، والسورة مكية

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.claim: The scale weighs deeds: faith and obedience have weight and standing with God, while disbelief and sins do not; the heavy deeds bring felicity and the light ones misery.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.anchor: الأعمال منها ما هو ثقيل في الميزان وهو ما له قدر ومنزلة عند الله وهو الإيمان وأنواع الطاعات

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.claim: The explanation of the scale has already been discussed in commentary on earlier surahs.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.anchor: وقد تقدم البحث عن معنى الميزان في تفسير السور السابقة

TABRISI:101:5-11/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:101:5-11/r3.claim: Light scales mean few good deeds and little obedience.

THALABI:v10p274#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p274#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p274#3/r5.claim: For the one whose scales are light, his destination and home are Hell.

THALABI:v10p274#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p274#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p274#3/r6.claim: He says hāwat ummuh is a familiar Arabic expression used when someone falls into a severe predicament.
THALABI:v10p274#3/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: هي كلمة عربية، كان الرجل إذا وقع في أمر شديد قال: هوت أمه

THALABI:v10p274#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p274#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v10p274#3/r7.claim: Some interpret ‘his mother’ as his head, meaning the people fall headfirst into Hell; Qatada and Abu Salih adopted this interpretation.
THALABI:v10p274#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أراد أم رأسه، يعني أنهم يهوون في النار على رؤوسهم

THALABI:v10p274#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p274#3/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v10p274#3/r8.claim: He reports an angel weighing each person’s deeds; a heavy scale brings a public proclamation of lasting felicity, while a light one brings lasting misery.
THALABI:v10p274#3/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: إن ملكا من ملائكة الله عز وجل موكل يوم القيامة بميزان ابن آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r7.claim: The person with light scales has evil deeds outweighing his good deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r7.anchor: {وأما من خفت موازينه} أي رجحت سيئاته على حسناته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.claim: Abu Bakr says their scales are heavy because they follow truth, which weighs heavily; a balance containing only truth should be heavy, while one holding falsehood should be light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.anchor: قال أبو بكر: إنما ثقلت موازينهم باتباعهم الحق، وثقلت (¬1) عليهم. وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يكون ثقيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.claim: Muqatil similarly says the truth is heavy and falsehood is light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.anchor: ونحو هذا ذكر مقاتل، وقال: لأن الحق ثقيل، والباطل خفيف

ELMALILI:101:8-11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r1.claim: Those with light scales either have no good deeds or have sins outweighing their good deeds.
ELMALILI:101:8-11/r1.anchor: hasenesi olmayan yahut seyyiâtı ağır basıp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.claim: Light deeds mean few or no good acts and imply sins outweighing them; the illustrative imagery teaches just judgment and responsible belief and conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r4.anchor: Amellerin hafif olması ise kulun dünyada yaptığı iyiliklerin azlığı veya bulunmaması demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.claim: Since afterlife events are unseen beyond what revelation states, one cannot speculate about how deeds will actually be weighed or measured.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.anchor: amellerin nasıl tartılacağı veya ölçüleceği hakkında söz söylemek yahut fikir yürütmek ise mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.claim: Those with few good deeds and many bad deeds go to Hell; commentators identify Hawiya as one of Hell's names.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r7.anchor: Tefsirlerde buradaki hâviye kelimesinin cehennemin isimlerinden biri olduğu belirtilmiştir

MUQATIL:101:9-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r3.claim: The scales are light because of the person's evil deeds; truth is heavy and wholesome, whereas falsehood is light and vile.
MUQATIL:101:9-11/r3.anchor: يقول: خفت موازينه بسيئاته وحق لميزان لا يقع فيه الحق أن يخف لأن الحق ثقيل مرىء، والباطل

QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.claim: This annihilation reading does not fit the later distinction of heavy and light scales; in God’s scale, rising and ascending count as weight, while descent is lightness: enduring righteous deeds matter most, and perishable pleasures have no weight.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.claim: Mawazin may mean deeds with weight before God or weighing scales; heaviness is their being outweighed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.anchor: الموازين : جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.claim: Abu Bakr told Umar that truth-followers' scales grow heavy through their conduct, while falsehood-followers' grow light; scales holding only good are rightly heavy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.anchor: ومنه حديث أبي بكر لعمر رضي الله عنهما في وصيته له : ( وإنما ثقلت موازين

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ALUSI:101:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r1.claim: The passage summarizes the division of people into two groups and signals each group's particular state after describing what is common to all.
ALUSI:101:6/r1.anchor: بيان إجمالي لتحزب الناس حزبين وتنبيه على كيفية الأحوال الخاصة بكل منهما أثر بيان الأحوال الشاملة للكل

ALUSI:101:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:8/r1.claim: The scales are light because the person has no good deed of consequence, or because his evil deeds outweigh his good ones.
ALUSI:101:8/r1.anchor: بأن لم يكن له حسنة يعتد بها أو ثقلت سيئآته على حسناته

BAGHAWI:101:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:101:8/r1.claim: The one whose scales are light is the one whose evil deeds outweigh the good.
BAGHAWI:101:8/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأما من خفت موازينه } رجحت سيئاته على حسناته

BAYDAWI:101:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:8/r1.claim: His scales are light because he has no good deed worthy of consideration.
BAYDAWI:101:8/r1.anchor: بأن لم يكن له حسنة يعبأ بها

BAYDAWI:101:8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:8/r2.claim: Alternatively, his evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

BIQAI:101:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:8/r1.claim: The scales are light or unsteady because his evil deeds predominate, or because he has no good deed through following falsehood.

BIQAI:101:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:8/r2.claim: Falsehood felt light to him in worldly life.

BIQAI:102:1/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:102:1/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:102:1/r1.claim: After al-Qāriʿa establishes the Hour, divides people into wretched and happy, and ends with the wretched, this sūra opens with the cause of misery to warn listeners away from it.
BIQAI:102:1/r1.anchor: لما أثبت في القارعة أمر الساعة

DURR:101:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:6/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:6/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:6/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:8/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:8/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:9/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r4.claim: Qatada identifies the light-scale person's Hāwiya as the Fire, their abode, mother, destination, and master.
DURR:101:9/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

IBNATIYYA:101:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r1.speaker: جمهور العلماء والفقهاء والمحدثين
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r1.claim: Most scholars, jurists, and hadith scholars affirm a literal balance on the Resurrection, with a beam, so people can understand divine judgment through a form they know and trust.
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r1.anchor: فقال جمهور العلماء والفقهاء والمحدثين : ميزان القيامة بعمود

IBNATIYYA:101:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r2.claim: Mujāhid denies a literal balance and takes it as a metaphor for justice, since a scale is the fairest measure known to people.
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد : ليس تم ميزان ؛ إنما هو العدل ، مثل ذكره بالميزان ؛ إذ هو أعدل ما يدري الناس

IBNATIYYA:101:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r3.claim: The plural balances are assigned to a person because that person has many different things to be weighed.
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r3.anchor: وجمعت الموازين للإنسان لما كانت له موزونات كثيرة متغايرة

IBNATIYYA:101:8/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r4.claim: A balance is heavy through faith and deeds, and light through their absence or scarcity; a believer’s balance will never be disastrously light.
IBNATIYYA:101:8/r4.anchor: وثقل هذا الميزان هو بالإيمان والأعمال ، وخفته بعدمها وقلتها ، ولن يخف خفة موبقة ميزان مؤمن

IBNKATHIR:101:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:101:8/r1.claim: Light scales mean that a person's bad deeds outweigh the good deeds.
IBNKATHIR:101:8/r1.anchor: { وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ } أي : رجحت سيئاته على حسناته

MAWARDI:101:8/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies Hawiya as Hell, called the person's mother because he takes refuge there as a child does with its mother; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poem supports the refuge sense.
MAWARDI:101:8/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الهاوية جهنم ،   سماها أُمَّا له ؛ لأنه يأوي إليها كما يأوي إلى أُمّه ،   قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI:101:8/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.claim: Hell is called Hawiya because the person falls into it, though it has a deep abyss.
MAWARDI:101:8/r2.anchor: وسميت النار هاوية ؛ لأنه يهوى فيها مع بعد قعرها .

MAWARDI:101:8/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.claim: ʿIkrima instead reads mother as the person's own head, upon which he falls into Hell; a poem addressed to ʿAmr illustrates this image.
MAWARDI:101:8/r3.anchor:
الثاني : أنه أراد أُمّ رأسه يهوي عليها في نار جهنم ،   قاله عكرمة . وقال الشاعر :
يا عَمروُ لو نَالَتْك أَرْحامُنا

MAWARDI:101:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:9/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI:101:9/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies Hawiya as Hell, called the person's mother because he takes refuge there as a child does with its mother; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poem supports the refuge sense.
MAWARDI:101:9/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن الهاوية جهنم ،   سماها أُمَّا له ؛ لأنه يأوي إليها كما يأوي إلى أُمّه ،   قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI:101:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:9/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:101:9/r2.claim: Hell is called Hawiya because the person falls into it, though it has a deep abyss.
MAWARDI:101:9/r2.anchor: وسميت النار هاوية ؛ لأنه يهوى فيها مع بعد قعرها .

MAWARDI:101:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:9/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI:101:9/r3.claim: ʿIkrima instead reads mother as the person's own head, upon which he falls into Hell; a poem addressed to ʿAmr illustrates this image.
MAWARDI:101:9/r3.anchor:
الثاني : أنه أراد أُمّ رأسه يهوي عليها في نار جهنم ،   قاله عكرمة . وقال الشاعر :
يا عَمروُ لو نَالَتْك أَرْحامُنا

NASAFI:101:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:101:8/r1.claim: The balances are light because their owners followed falsehood.
NASAFI:101:8/r1.anchor: { وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ موازينه } باتباعهم الباطل .

RAZI:101:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:101:6/r1.claim: On describing the Resurrection, God divides people into two groups according to the heaviness or lightness of their scales.
RAZI:101:6/r1.anchor: لما وصف يوم القيامة قسم الناس فيه إلى قسمين

RAZI:101:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:101:6/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes mawāzīn as the plural of mawzūn, meaning a deed with weight and worth before God; he compares it to saying one thing is by the measure or weight of another.
RAZI:101:6/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء قال : ونظيره يقال : عندي درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك

RAZI:101:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:101:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the word as balances with a tongue and two pans: obedient people's good deeds appear beautiful and, if they outweigh, lead to Paradise; unbelievers' evil deeds appear ugly and light, leading to the Fire.
RAZI:101:6/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الميزان له لسان وكفتان لا يوزن فيه إلا الأعمال فيؤتى بحسنات المطيع في أحسن صورة

RAZI:101:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:101:6/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the balance has two pans but does not describe it further.
RAZI:101:6/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن : في الميزان له كفتان ولا يوصف

RAZI:101:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r5.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI:101:6/r5.claim: The theologians say deeds themselves cannot be weighed, especially after ceasing to exist; instead, records may be weighed, light and darkness may signify good and evil, or the records may be embodied beautifully or hideously, publicly revealing people's standing.
RAZI:101:6/r5.anchor: قال المتكلمون : إن نفس الحسنات والسيئات لا يصح وزنهما

RAZI:101:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:101:8/r1.claim: The scales are light because a person's good deeds are few, so the evil deeds outweigh them.
RAZI:101:8/r1.anchor: أي قلت : حسناته فرجحت السيئات على الحسنات

RAZI:101:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:8/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
RAZI:101:8/r2.claim: Abū Bakr says scales are heavy when people follow truth and bear its weight in worldly life, and light when they follow falsehood and its ease; a scale containing only truth is rightly heavy, one holding falsehood rightly light.
RAZI:101:8/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه : إنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينه باتباعهم الحق في الدنيا وثقله عليهم

RAZI:101:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:8/r3.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:101:8/r3.claim: Muqātil says truth itself is heavy while falsehood is light.
RAZI:101:8/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل : إنما كان كذلك لأن الحق ثقيل والباطل خفيف
